full_judgment: 8. The argument is attractive but if section 19(1)(a) is read with section 180) of the Ordinance, it can hardly be accepted. Section 18(5) makes it very clear that the deposit is to be made "within the time specified" in section 19. The element of time referred to In section 19(1)(a) therefore acquires a mandatory character in view of the provisions of section 18(5) The petitioner may have filed his application for permission to deposit rent within time but it is not the application simplicity which has to be filed within time, it is the deposit u/s. 19(1) (a) which is prima required to be filed within the time fixed Section 19(5) provides that a deposit sit be accompanied by an application stating tarn particulars. It was not enough that the: application mentioned in section 19(5) was filed within time. It is mandatory that the deposit must also be filed within time. From the order of the Controller dated 9.8.77. It does not transpire that he permitted the petitioner to make the deposit after 13.8.77. Indeed, in the absence of any legislation making section 5 of the Limitation Act applicable to a deposit of rent u/s 19(1)(a) of the Ordinance It is net even permissible for the Controller to extend time of the deposit. The Controller, in fact, permitted the petitioner to file the chalan on 22.8.77. If the petitioner wanted to avail of the benefits of section 18(1) of the Ordinance he was to make the deposit on or within 13.8.77. He having not done so clearly defaulted In making the deposit within the time allowed by the Ordinance and I find no error of law apparent on the face of the record in the decision of the learned Additional District Judge that the petitioner's deposit is time barred.
